title: OpenAI's claimed ten open-problem math solutions from an unreleased model
reason: OpenAI posted 2026-08-01 that an internal, unreleased model it calls 'Astra' (confirmed as OpenAI's own internal codename via an identifiable OpenAI staff X post, not press paraphrase) produced results on ten long-standing open problems in mathematics and theoretical computer science (sphere packing, non-sofic groups, arithmetic circuit complexity, lattice cryptography, etc.), each with a Lean proof certificate. Cycle 3 verifier sub-agent confirmed the GitHub artifact (github.com/openai/ten-proofs) is real: public openai org repo, Apache-2.0, Lean 4 with mathlib, 10 named .lean files matching the claimed results, plus a separate ComparatorChallenges checking harness -- this is a genuine, structurally plausible research artifact, not vaporware. What is NOT yet independently confirmed: (a) whether the Lean proofs actually type-check/build cleanly -- verifier could not run `lake build` within budget; (b) any independent mathematician's assessment that the ten problems are genuinely long-standing-open as framed, or that the proofs are correct -- searches surfaced only secondary paraphrase, no primary quote from a named mathematician, and a Hacker News technical thread could not be fetched (rate-limited); (c) OpenAI's own post itself already discloses human/org involvement in formalizing the Lean proofs ('helped prepare the manuscripts and formalize the proofs ... taking responsibility for their correctness'), so this is not framed by OpenAI itself as a fully autonomous result. Decisive reason to hold rather than publish as a labeled vendor-claim this cycle: the same lab has a directly analogous prior incident in this exact claim category -- OpenAI VP Kevin Weil posted and then deleted an 'AI solved 10 Erdos problems' claim in October 2025 that mathematician Thomas Bloom debunked as a literature-search artifact, not new math (see https://techcrunch.com/2025/10/19/openais-embarrassing-math/). Given that precedent, publishing this new ten-problems claim -- even labeled vendor-claim -- without at least one independent mathematician's read is judged too easy to mistake for confirmed mathematics, and not worth the residual reputational risk of publish-then-correct on a front-page-scale claim. Holding one more cycle for a cheap, high-value check (an HN/MathOverflow read, one mathematician-focused search) is a better tradeoff than lowering the bar under this cycle's time pressure.
watch: Any independent mathematician (e.g. via MathOverflow, Hacker News technical discussion, a named academic's blog/X post) assessing whether the ten problems are genuinely long-standing-open as framed and whether the proofs look sound
Confirmation the github.com/openai/ten-proofs Lean files actually build/type-check (or a report that they do not)
Any dispute, correction, or retraction of this specific 2026-08-01 post, echoing the October 2025 Kevin Weil Erdos-problems retraction
Coverage from a Tier 0-2 outlet with its own named-author analysis rather than a relay of OpenAI's post
